title: Punjab government employees and roadways workers strike in Chandigarh

tea.why: Government employees and transport workers are protesting over pending pay, pension, and regularisation demands.
tea.want: Release of pending dearness allowance, restoration of the Old Pension Scheme, and regularisation of contractual staff.
tea.changed: Oct 22: Negotiations between employee representatives and state officials remained inconclusive after two hours.

summary: Hundreds of thousands of government employees and contractual roadways workers took mass casual leave and extended strikes across Punjab, gathering in large numbers in Chandigarh and outside deputy commissioners' offices in all districts. The protests disrupted public transport and paralysed government offices, while healthcare institutions faced difficulties outside of emergency services. The agitation is spearheaded by unions including the Joint Action Committee, Sanjha Mullazam Manch, and Sanjha Mullazam Front. Their demands include the release of pending dearness allowance instalments and arrears, the restoration of the Old Pension Scheme, the regularisation of contractual staff, and the implementation of a cashless health scheme. State officials met with employee delegations, but negotiations remained inconclusive after authorities clarified that certain temporary teachers received tenure rather than regular status with full financial benefits. Union leaders criticized a government order declaring the mass casual leave unauthorised.
organizers: Punjab Roadways, PUNBUS and PRTC Contract Workers' Union
demands: Release of pending dearness allowance instalments and arrears
Restoration of the Old Pension Scheme
Regularisation of contractual and outsourced staff
Implementation of the cashless health scheme
response: The state government declared the mass casual leave 'unauthorised leave of absence'. Chief Secretary KAP Sinha and other officials held meetings with employee delegations, though negotiations remained inconclusive.

crowd.text: over 3 lakh staff taking mass casual leave

updates.text: Employee representatives met Chief Secretary KAP Sinha, but the meeting remained inconclusive after two hours of negotiations.
